hero.title: The problem defines the engineering team.
hero.intro: SDK brings together the specialists a system actually requires, coordinates their work and remains accountable for delivery quality. Start with one technical decision or give us a defined workstream to own.

navigator.heading: Start with the pressure on the system.
navigator.intro: A useful engagement starts with the constraint, not a catalogue of technologies.

items.title: Modernize
items.copy: Reduce the risk and cost of changing software that can no longer keep accumulating patches.

items.title: Build
items.copy: Design and deliver backend platforms, integrations and product systems around a clear operating need.

items.title: Automate
items.copy: Put AI into a real workflow with the data, evaluation and operational controls it needs.

items.title: Stabilize
items.copy: Find the causes behind reliability, deployment, performance or data-flow problems.

items.title: Diagnose
items.copy: Turn an unclear technical situation into evidence, options and a defensible next decision.

capabilities.heading: Engineering depth, organized around the decision in front of you.
capabilities.intro: Each capability can stand alone or combine with others when the system crosses boundaries.

items.title: Change an aging system without losing what still works.
items.situation: The system matters to the business, but upgrades are risky, delivery is slowing down or too much knowledge sits in undocumented behavior.
investigation: Dependencies, runtime constraints and unsupported components
Data flows, integrations and hidden operational coupling
Change risk, test coverage and migration boundaries
delivery: Current-state assessment and prioritized modernization plan
items.firstStep: Map what the system does today, where change is dangerous and which boundary can move first.

items.title: Build the parts of the product that carry the business rules.
items.situation: A product needs APIs, integrations, authorization, asynchronous work or realtime behavior that must remain understandable as requirements change.
investigation: Domain boundaries, users and access rules
Integration contracts, failure modes and data ownership
Operational volume, latency and consistency requirements
delivery: Backend services, APIs and integration layers
Queues, events and realtime application flows
items.firstStep: Define the business boundary, the data it owns and the failure conditions the design must tolerate.

items.title: Move AI from a convincing demo into an accountable workflow.
items.situation: A manual process is expensive or slow, but an AI feature will only be useful if its inputs, outputs, evaluation and fallback behavior are controlled.
investigation: Workflow decisions that require a model and those that do not
Source data, permissions and retrieval quality
Evaluation criteria, human review and failure handling
delivery: LLM integrations, agents and workflow automation
items.firstStep: Choose one workflow, define an acceptable result and measure the current human process before automating it.

items.title: Make production behavior visible before changing capacity.
items.situation: Deployments are fragile, incidents are hard to explain, infrastructure costs are unclear or the system is approaching an operational limit.
investigation: Deployment path, environments and recovery procedures
Logs, metrics, traces and incident evidence
Resource constraints, bottlenecks and scaling assumptions
items.firstStep: Establish what the system is doing under real load and how the team currently detects and recovers from failure.

items.title: Connect data, operations and the people using the system.
items.situation: The product needs a dependable data path and an interface that makes complex operational work easier to understand and complete.
investigation: Data ownership, lifecycle, search and access patterns
User tasks, decision points and error recovery
Server and browser boundaries that affect performance
delivery: Data models, search, cache and ingestion flows
Operational web interfaces and internal tooling
items.firstStep: Follow one critical user task from source data to final decision and identify where context is lost.

engagements.heading: Match the commitment to what is already known.
engagements.intro: An uncertain system needs evidence before a responsible implementation commitment. A defined outcome can move directly into a focused workstream.

options.title: Technical assessment
options.bestFor: A consequential decision where the current state, risk or implementation path is unclear.
options.output: Evidence, options, risks and a prioritized recommendation the client can use with or without SDK.
options.commitment: A bounded investigation with agreed access, questions and deliverables.

options.title: Engineering workstream
options.bestFor: A defined technical outcome that needs a composed team and clear delivery ownership.
options.output: Working changes, reviewed decisions, deployment evidence and documentation for the agreed scope.
options.commitment: A focused delivery period with visible checkpoints and acceptance criteria.

options.title: Technical partnership
options.bestFor: A system that needs staged modernization or continued ownership of a technical workstream.
options.output: A maintained roadmap, incremental delivery and an operating record of decisions, risks and progress.
options.commitment: A continuing engagement reviewed against an agreed workstream and priorities.

teamModel.heading: Specialists selected for the system. One company accountable to the client.
teamModel.body: SDK works with independent engineering specialists. We compose the team around the problem, coordinate the work and set the quality framework for the engagement. The client does not need to recruit, align and manage a collection of unrelated contributors.

steps.title: Define the need
steps.copy: Clarify the system, constraints, decisions and outcome before deciding who should do the work.

steps.title: Compose the team
steps.copy: Select the disciplines and experience relevant to the engagement instead of forcing it into a fixed bench.

steps.title: Control quality
steps.copy: Use visible decisions, reviews, acceptance criteria and operational evidence throughout delivery.

steps.title: Transfer ownership
steps.copy: Keep code, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge in the client’s control.

cta.title: You do not need to arrive with a finished specification.
cta.body: Describe the system, the pressure on it and the decision you need to make. We will start by determining whether SDK is a useful fit.
cta.label: Discuss the problem
